decisions.title: 3-layer memory write enforcement
decisions.context: Agents completed tasks but left decision-log, progress, and patterns.json empty across sessions. Dashboard showed no historical data despite days of active usage. No automatic mechanism existed to enforce memory writes.
decisions.decision: Implement 3-layer enforcement: (1) 4 helper scripts in .claude/scripts/ — add-decision.sh, add-task.sh, add-pattern.sh, update-context.sh. (2) 5 mandatory trigger events defined in CLAUDE.md with explicit timing and output format. (3) Cross-session debt hook — on-session-stop.sh detects empty files and writes .memory-debt.md; on-user-prompt.sh at next session start injects the reminder then deletes it. Debt fires exactly once per missed session.
decisions.rationale: No automatic mechanism existed to write semantic memory files — helper scripts + CLAUDE.md triggers + cross-session debt hook ensures compliance

positive: Memory files stay populated across sessions without manual intervention
Dashboard always shows real data from day one of usage
Cross-session amnesia eliminated — debt hook catches omissions and fires exactly once
negative: Each task completion requires AgentX to run an extra shell command before moving on
risks: Scripts must exist at expected paths or enforcement silently fails — mitigated by init.sh pre-flight check

decisions.title: Index-based onclick for session modal
decisions.context: Session Activity modal showed blank prompts despite correct data in llm-usage.json. Root cause: onclick='openSessionModal(${JSON.stringify(s).replace(/"/g, """)})' — user prompt text containing quotes, newlines, or template literals corrupted the JS object literal embedded in the HTML attribute. Bug was silent — no error, just blank modal.
decisions.decision: Store rendered sessions in window._safetyTabSessions[] before .map(). Pass numeric index i in onclick string. Handler checks typeof s === 'number' and retrieves window._safetyTabSessions[i]. No serialization or encoding required anywhere in the flow.
decisions.rationale: JSON-in-attribute encoding (replacing " with ") is fragile — any special char in prompt text corrupts the JS object. Solution: store sessions in window._safetyTabSessions[], pass index i in onclick. Zero encoding needed.

positive: Prompts with any special characters (quotes, JSON, code snippets) render correctly
Simpler code — removed all encoding/decoding logic entirely
Modal works for all session types including those with multi-line or structured prompts
risks: Global array must be assigned before any card is clicked — mitigated by assigning before .map() call, never after

decisions.title: Per-file line counts with heat-map in SAFETY tab
decisions.context: Files Modified list in session modal showed only filenames — no indication of change magnitude. A one-line typo fix looked identical to a 500-line architectural rewrite. No visual signal to identify high-risk sessions worth reviewing.
decisions.decision: Switch track-usage.sh from git diff --name-only to git diff --numstat HEAD. Build {path, added, removed} objects per file using a jq loop. Dashboard applies heat-map background colors: green rgba(16,185,129,0.08) for <10 lines changed, yellow for 10–50, red for >50, purple for rewrites (>200 total or removed/added ratio >70%). Binary files return '-' from numstat — handled with jq's tonumber? // 0 fallback.
decisions.rationale: git diff --numstat captures added/removed lines per file as {path,added,removed} objects. Dashboard renders heat-map: green<10, yellow 10-50, red>50, purple=rewrite(>200 or removed/added>70%). Backwards compatible: old string[] sessions still render.

positive: Visual indicator of change magnitude — identify risky sessions at a glance without opening files
High deletion-rate rewrites flagged in purple — signals sessions worth reviewing for regressions
Zero migration effort for existing 42 sessions — old string[] format renders filename-only gracefully
negative: Binary files (images, compiled assets) always show +0/-0 — misleading for asset-heavy sessions

decisions.title: Backwards-compatible schema evolution for activity.files
decisions.context: Changing activity.files from string[] to object[] {path, added, removed} would break all 42 existing session entries in llm-usage.json. A migration script risked corrupting historical session data — the only source of truth for past activity.
decisions.decision: Dashboard renderer detects format per entry with typeof f === 'object'. Old string[] entries render filename only (legacy display). New object entries render filename + +N/-M with heat-map colors. track-usage.sh writes new format for all sessions going forward. Existing sessions untouched — migration is lazy on read, not on write.
decisions.rationale: Changed activity.files from string[] to object[] {path,added,removed}. Dashboard detects format with typeof f==='object' and renders accordingly. Old sessions show filename only; new sessions show +N/-M with color. No migration needed.

positive: Zero risk to historical data — 42 existing sessions remain readable and correctly displayed
No migration script needed — eliminates one-time data corruption window
New sessions immediately show rich format without any transition period
negative: Two rendering code paths in dashboard.html must be maintained as long as old sessions exist
risks: Future schema changes to activity.files must extend the typeof check pattern — risk of forgetting and breaking old sessions again

_comments.dateFormat: Use ISO 8601 format with timezone for timestamps: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS-05:00
_comments.note: Dashboard will display date and time when timestamp includes 'T', otherwise only date
